records.title: The Employment Situation, August 2026
records.quote: Total nonfarm payroll employment increased by 162,000 in August, and the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.1 percent
records.about: The government's monthly jobs report: the Bureau of Labor Statistics counts payroll jobs through a survey of employers and measures unemployment through a survey of households, and publishes both in this release. Our copy was saved the day it came out.

records.title: Total nonfarm payrolls, monthly

records.title: U-6 underemployment rate, monthly
records.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), from BLS
records.about: The broadest measure of slack: the unemployed plus people who want work but stopped looking plus people working part time because they could not find full-time work.

records.title: Prime-age (25 to 54) participation, monthly
records.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), from BLS

The Real Earnings report for August comes out with the September 11 inflation release; this page uses the year-over-year wage growth from the payroll survey instead and says so.
Three outlets quote three different surveys (53,000, 56,000, 65,000); each is attributed to its outlet and poll rather than treated as one number.

sources_admitted.evidence: BLS release copied from the September 4 capture run (bls_employment_situation source, receipt in that run); FRED and ALFRED CSVs fetched September 8 and saved under dated names; eight coverage articles copied from the same capture run; all listed in data/sources/SOURCES.md with bytes and sha256.

derived_numbers_computed.evidence: Monthly changes, the three-in-twelve count, the 3-, 12-month and yearly averages, the revisions table and wage growth recomputed on September 8 from PAYEMS-2026-09-04.csv, the two ALFRED vintages and CES0500000003-2026-09-04.csv; values live in src/data/jobs202608.mjs.

outlet_claims_verified.evidence: Seven articles checked line by line against the release text: Al Jazeera health care 12,000 vs release 13,000; UPI workweek 0.1 percent vs release 0.1 hour; PBS yearly averages recomputed and matched; CNBC 58 vs Al Jazeera 60 percent odds at different times of day.
